row.evidence: Jenkins is 'the leading open source automation server'; its security docs offer only security realms (own user database, LDAP, SAML/OIDC SSO via plugins) and the Jenkins plugin index returns no SCIM plugin.
row.notes: Free, self-hosted open-source project with no paid tiers, so there is no SCIM tax to measure. Identity comes from a configurable security realm: Jenkins' own user database, LDAP (users and groups delegated to the directory), or SAML/OIDC SSO through plugins. No SCIM endpoint is documented in the Jenkins handbook and plugins.jenkins.io returns no plugin for 'scim'. Okta's 'Jenkins' OIN app is SAML only. Commercial Jenkins distributions (e.g. CloudBees CI) are separate vendors and were not researched here.

plans.name: Jenkins (open source)
plans.notes: SSO needs the SAML (or OIDC) plugin.

scim.notes: Not stated as 'no' by Jenkins; no SCIM endpoint or plugin was found in the handbook's security realms or the plugin index (search 'scim' returned 0).

user_api.notes: Jenkins' Remote Access API page documents job and build operations; no user-management endpoints were found there.

okta.notes: OIN 'Jenkins' page marks only SAML as checked (read from page markup).

fallbacks.other_sync: LDAP security realm delegates users and groups to the directory (authentication-time lookup, not provisioning).
